rubric.statement: `Adapter.format` treats a `dspy.History` input specially: it looks for an input field whose annotation is exactly `History` and only takes the conversation-history path when that field exists.

When a history field is present, DSPy removes it from the signature with `signature.delete(history_field_name)` and deletes it from `inputs`, so the history object itself is not left to be serialized into the live current-turn payload.
`format_conversation_history` expands `inputs[history_field_name].messages` into real earlier chat turns by appending one `user` message and one `assistant` message for each saved exchange.
After the reconstructed history turns, `Adapter.format` appends the current invocation as a fresh final `user` message rather than folding it into the prior history.

The outbound message list still starts with a system message built from the original signature, and the regression test shows one saved exchange being sent as `system`, prior `user`, prior `assistant`, then current `user`.
